analysis.investment_thesis: Capillary Technologies is a loss-making B2B SaaS company that has only just turned marginally profitable (INR 13 Cr net profit in FY2025 after four consecutive loss years) and is priced at 420x earnings — a combination I find deeply unattractive. It sits entirely outside my circle of competence and violates nearly every financial quality threshold I require before committing capital.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 36.7% (2021→2025) shows strong topline momentum in a growing loyalty-SaaS niche
Net cash positive balance sheet — cash of INR 201 Cr exceeds total debt of INR 106 Cr, D/E at 0.17
EBITDA turned solidly positive in FY2025 (INR 72 Cr) after years of deep losses — business model is improving
key_risks: P/E of 420x is not valuation — it is speculation; my comfort zone is 12-20x for quality businesses
ROE of 2.56% and ROCE of 2.88% are deeply sub-standard; I need >15% ROE before I even look further
Free cash flow was -INR 94 Cr in FY2025 despite reported profit — the business still burns cash and lacks earnings quality
red_flags: Four consecutive years of net losses (2021–2024: -23, -101, -88, -57 Cr) — a chronic cash-burning history
Operating CF turned sharply negative in FY2025 (-46 Cr) even as accounting profit appeared — divergence is a red flag
No dividend history — consistent with a business that has never generated real, distributable earnings
B2B enterprise tech is outside my domain; I do not invest in businesses I cannot understand from a customer behavior standpoint
Promoter stake at 52.23% — below my 55% preference threshold, with no visible upward trend
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my perspective, Capillary Technologies fails on almost every criterion I care about. The company reported its first-ever net profit of just INR 13 Cr in FY2025 — against a market cap of INR 4,492 Cr — implying a P/E of 420x. I have never paid more than 20x earnings for any business, and I never will. The ROE of 2.56% and ROCE of 2.88% tell me that the business is earning almost nothing on the capital deployed. Even with a generous view of the improving EBITDA trajectory (INR 72 Cr in FY2025 vs. losses in prior years), the operating cash flow was -INR 46 Cr in FY2025 — meaning the reported profit is not showing up in cash. That disconnect worries me deeply.

The revenue growth of 36.7% CAGR looks exciting, but I have learned over decades that fast-growing, loss-making technology companies are dangerous for conservative investors. The capex is rising (INR 47 Cr in FY2025), free cash flow is deeply negative (-INR 94 Cr), and the business has never paid a dividend. This is not a compounder — it is a growth story where the market is paying a very high price for a future that may or may not arrive. My style is to own businesses like DMart, where I can predict demand, understand the customer, and see steady, durable cash generation. Capillary Technologies is the opposite of that. I would not touch this at any price close to current levels.
